issues.t: Oil sludge leading to engine failure
issues.sym: Ticking or knocking from the engine, an oil pressure light that flickers at idle, low idle speed, and in bad cases the engine shuts off or seizes while driving, often around 80,000 to 100,000 miles.
issues.why: The 2.7L V6 is widely known for building up thick oil sludge that blocks oil passages and starves the bearings and timing chain. Long oil-change intervals and heat make it worse, and a leaking internal water pump can add coolant to the oil.
issues.next: Change the oil and filter every 3,000 to 5,000 miles with a quality oil, and watch the oil light. If you hear knocking or the oil light flickers, stop driving and have oil pressure checked. A failed engine usually means a replacement engine.

issues.t: Internal water pump leaks coolant into the oil
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle under the car, a sweet smell, milky or foamy oil on the dipstick, overheating, or the engine stalling or seizing.
issues.why: On the 2.7L the water pump sits inside the engine behind the timing cover and is driven by the timing chain. When its seal fails, coolant can leak straight into the oil, ruining the bearings.
issues.next: If coolant is disappearing or the oil looks milky, stop driving and have the cooling system pressure tested. Replacing the pump means removing the timing cover, so most shops replace the timing chain parts at the same time.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch or breakage
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine, a check engine light, rough running, or the engine suddenly quitting and refusing to restart. A broken chain can bend the valves.
issues.why: Sludge and poor oil flow wear the 2.7L's timing chain, guides and tensioners, and metal debris in the oil is often found with a stretched chain.
issues.next: Have any new rattle checked right away. Catching a stretched chain before it breaks keeps the repair to the timing parts instead of a cylinder head or engine.

issues.t: Engine knocking and bearing failure
issues.sym: A deep knock from the engine that gets louder with speed, often followed by complete engine failure around 100,000 miles.
issues.why: Restricted oil flow from sludge wears the bearings on the 2.7L V6. Engine failure is the most-reported problem on these years.
issues.next: Stop driving when you hear a deep knock and have oil pressure checked. Most cars with a failed bottom end get a replacement engine.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping, harsh shifting or failure
issues.sym: Slipping between gears, delayed or harsh shifts, the car stuck in one gear (limp mode), refusal to shift out of first, or no drive at all.
issues.why: The front-drive automatic used in these cars wears internally, and solenoid, servo and torque converter faults are commonly reported. Old or low fluid speeds up the wear.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and have codes read. Chrysler requires its own ATF+4-type fluid, so make sure the shop uses the right one. A slipping unit usually needs a rebuild or a remanufactured transmission.

issues.t: Steering rack and tie rod wear
issues.sym: Clunking or creaking when turning, especially when cold, loose or wandering steering, a car that won't hold an alignment, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Worn steering rack mounting bushings, inner tie rods and the rack itself are among the most reported complaints on these LH-platform cars.
issues.next: Have the rack mounts and tie rods inspected for play. Worn parts make the car harder to control, so do not put this off. A rack replacement is followed by an alignment.

issues.t: Stalling or no-start from cam or crank sensor
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, stalls while driving or at a stop, or stumbles, often with a check engine light.
issues.why: A failing camshaft or crankshaft position sensor, or damaged wiring to it, stops the computer from knowing engine position.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Test the wiring and connector too, not just the sensor, so the problem doesn't come back.

issues.t: Oil pressure light flickers at idle
issues.sym: The oil light flickers or comes on at idle or when stopped, then goes out when you press the gas.
issues.why: Low oil pressure at idle is often an early sign of sludge or worn bearings in the 2.7L V6, though a bad sender can also cause it.
issues.next: Check the oil level now. Have a mechanic measure real oil pressure with a gauge before assuming it is just the sensor.

issues.t: Timing belt failure if replacement is overdue
issues.sym: No warning in most cases: the engine suddenly quits and won't restart. Because these engines are interference designs, the valves can be damaged.
issues.why: The 3.2L and 3.5L V6 use a rubber timing belt with a 100,000-mile factory interval. A belt that is overdue can snap.
issues.next: If your car is near or past 100,000 miles with no record of a belt change, have it replaced along with the water pump and tensioner.

issues.t: Coolant leak from heater tube O-ring
issues.sym: Coolant dripping at the front of the engine, a low coolant level, or a sweet smell after driving.
issues.why: On the 3.2L and 3.5L the front heater tube O-ring hardens with age, and the metal tube can rust through from the inside.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have the leak found. Replace the tube and O-ring together.

issues.t: Overheating from worn water pump impeller
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, especially in traffic, even though no leak is visible.
issues.why: The water pump on the 3.2L and 3.5L has a plastic impeller that can erode from rust and sediment, so it moves less coolant.
issues.next: Stop if the gauge goes into the red. Have the cooling system pressure tested and the pump checked; it is usually replaced with the timing belt.

issues.t: Power door locks stop working
issues.sym: One or more doors won't lock or unlock with the switch or remote, sometimes with a buzzing or grinding from inside the door.
issues.why: The electric door lock actuators wear out.
issues.next: Lock the affected door by hand for now. Replacing the actuator in that door fixes it.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold
issues.sym: The air conditioning suddenly blows warm air, or needs recharging again and again.
issues.why: Refrigerant leaks and A/C compressor or condenser failures are commonly reported.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested with dye rather than just recharged, so the failed part is found.

issues.t: Door weatherstripping shrinks and falls off
issues.sym: Wind whistle at highway speed, more road noise, water getting in, or rubber seals peeling away from the door.
issues.why: The door seals shrink and harden with age.
issues.next: Replace the worn seals. Glue only works as a short-term fix.

issues.t: Cracked dashboard
issues.sym: Cracks open in the top of the dash, often above the glove box or toward the windshield.
issues.why: The dashboard cover cracks with heat and age.
issues.next: A dash cover or cap hides the crack. Full dashboard replacement is a big job because the passenger airbag area is involved.

issues.t: Head gasket failure on older V6 engines
issues.sym: Overheating, coolant loss, white exhaust smoke, or oil and coolant mixing.
issues.why: Owners of high-mileage 1996-1997 LH cars report blown head gaskets, often after the engine has overheated.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats. A cooling system pressure test and combustion leak test will confirm it.

issues.t: Pinched rear defroster wire can cause a fire
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke near the rear window or trunk area, or the rear defroster stops working.
issues.why: Owners report the wire feeding the rear window defroster can be pinched and short out.
issues.next: Stop using the rear defroster if you smell burning and have the wiring inspected.

issues.t: Fuel rail can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell under the hood or wetness around the fuel injectors.
issues.why: On cars with the 3.5L engine, the fuel rail O-rings can leak or the plastic rail can crack, a fire risk. Chrysler recalled them to reinforce or replace the rail.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive the car. Have a dealer check that this recall was done.

issues.t: Shifter interlock can let the car roll away (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter can be moved out of Park with the key out, or the key can come out when the shifter is not in Park.
issues.why: The ignition-park interlock in the floor shifter can fail. Chrysler recalled cars to install a new push rod in the shifter.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake, and have a dealer confirm the recall was completed.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: On some 1998 cars the passenger airbag might not deploy in a crash. Chrysler recalled them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the repair done.

issues.t: Front seat back can suddenly recline (recall)
issues.sym: The front seat back drops backward while driving.
issues.why: The recliner bolts in the front seat can break. Chrysler recalled cars to replace the bolts.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the recall status; the fix is free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag has the wrong inflator charge (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; the passenger airbag may not protect correctly in a crash.
issues.why: Some passenger airbag inflators were built with the wrong charge amount. The airbag module is replaced under recall.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have it done.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can make brakes drag (recall)
issues.sym: Brakes that drag, a burning smell from the wheels, or brakes that fade after heavy use.
issues.why: On some cars without ABS, a snap ring in the master cylinder was bent during assembly and can hold the brakes partly on. The master cylinder is replaced under recall.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the recall status, especially if the brakes feel like they are dragging.

issues.t: Seat belt mounting bolts may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: Some seat belt mounting bolts may not withstand crash forces. They are replaced under recall.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Driver seat belt retractor may not protect fully (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: On some cars the driver's seat belt retractor may give less protection in a frontal crash. It is replaced under recall.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Child seat anchors may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; a child seat may not stay properly attached in a crash.
issues.why: The child seat anchor system did not meet the federal standard, so Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If you use a child seat, have a dealer confirm this recall was done.
